neighbours.label: the raising verb 'seem/seemed' after a subject (how someone appears)
fire: After the long meeting the managers seemed exhausted and irritable.
Our new neighbours seem friendly, though we rarely see them.
At the trial the witnesses seemed nervous when they spoke.
Many of the younger nurses seem eager to work night shifts.
During the final quarter the visiting team seemed to lose focus.
Some children seem to pick up languages without any effort.
In the photos the two brothers seemed happy and relaxed.
Most of the voters we interviewed seemed unsure about the plan.
quiet: After the long meeting the managers were exhausted and irritable.
Our new neighbours are friendly, though we rarely see them.
At the trial the witnesses spoke nervously when questioned.
Many of the younger nurses want to work night shifts.
During the final quarter the visiting team lost its focus.
Some children pick up languages without any effort.
In the photos the two brothers were smiling and relaxed.
Most of the voters we interviewed were unsure about the plan.
